title: FALSIFIER, NOW SPLIT because the original conflated an architectural claim with an environmental one. (A) ARCHITECTURAL
description: FALSIFIER, NOW SPLIT because the original conflated an architectural claim with an environmental one. (A) ARCHITECTURAL — SATISFIED: a peer outside the docker bridge obtains a circuit reservation and completes a federated resolve when the relay's listen port is published on the host and it announces a host-routable address. (B) ENVIRONMENTAL — NOT SATISFIED HERE: the announced address is not RFC1918. || EVIDENCE FOR (A), measured: a relay was started in its own container with -p 30333:30333 and PUBLIC_IP set to the host's LAN address. It announced /ip4/10.0.0.104/tcp/30333/p2p/12D3KooWLvbz9cQddY2q8DZLYUMQ3ZQqJEAZXrERP7s15aMRREto -- host-routable rather than docker-internal. A TCP probe from the HOST namespace to 10.0.0.104:30333 connected, where the previous docker-internal relay at 172.17.0.2:30333 was refused (the host routes 172.17/16 via the default gateway, not the bridge). federation-hub-e2e.ts then ran FROM THE HOST and passed the full loop: reserved a circuit on the relay, registered spoke_probe into hub discovery (HTTP 201), discovery echoed the circuit multiaddr, and a second node resolved the shape through the relay. That exact harness, from that exact vantage, previously failed with 'ingress got no circuit reservation'. So federation is no longer bounded by the docker bridge, and the mechanism -- publish the port, announce a routable address -- is proven. || WHY (B) REMAINS OPEN AND IS NOT CLOSABLE BY CODE: 10.0.0.104 is RFC1918, so this proves reachability for peers on the same LAN, not for peers on the internet. The original falsifier explicitly required a non-RFC1918 announced address, and satisfying it needs a host with a public address -- an environmental input, not an architectural change. Closing on the LAN result would be closing on a technicality against my own recorded predicate. || REMAINING WORK is therefore deployment, not design: run the relay somewhere with a public address (deploy-hub.sh already does this on a VM) and re-run the same harness from a genuinely external vantage. The substrate-live relay itself still announces 172.17.0.2 and has 30333 unpublished; changing that needs a container recreate, which is why a separate published relay was used to prove the mechanism.
